name: Anaphora Resolution
description: Analyzes the frequency of pronoun versus explicit noun usage for coreference
mechanism: This method studies how a text handles anaphora—the use of pronouns (e.g., 'it', 'they', 'she') to refer back to previously established nouns. Humans unconsciously rely heavily on anaphora because our cognitive context smoothly carries the reference forward. However, LLMs (due to their self-attention mechanisms and safety training focused on absolute clarity) often exhibit 'anaphora avoidance'. They have a statistically higher tendency to explicitly repeat the core noun ('The company announced...', 'The company stated...', 'The company's goal...') instead of using pronouns ('it', 'its'). By tracking the ratio of explicit coreferences to anaphoric pronouns, this system exposes the overly-cautious structural scaffolding typical of machine generation.
parameters:
Analysis type: Syntactic Coreference Tracking
Media: Text
Input: Raw text string
Minimum length: 200 words
Output: Explicit coreference ratio (0-100)
Processing: Dependency parsing and NER
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-82%. Very effective in identifying 'corporate style' or overly formal AI summaries.
source: Cognitive grammar and self-attention dependency bias research.
useCase: Detecting text generated by LLMs that prioritize absolute sentence-level clarity by avoiding natural human pronoun usage.
strengths:
• Targets the fundamental self-attention nature of transformer models
• Highly effective on narrative and informative texts
• Subtle enough that standard humanizing prompts fail to bypass it
limitations:
• Susceptible to human writers drafting legal or highly formal technical documents
• Requires heavy NLP coreference resolution models
• Performance drops significantly on short texts

references.title: Manning, C.D. & Schütze, H. (1999). Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing. MIT Press.
